Introduction

General

(EIAO) (Cap. 499).

4.2.2.2 The NCO also provides statutory control on general construction works during
restricted hours (i.e. between 1900 and 0700 hours and any time on a general holiday,

works during restricted hours would require a Construction Noise Permit (CNP). The
GW-TM details the procedures for assessing such application. The granting of a CNP
is subject to the contemporary conditions and it may be revoked at any time for failure
to comply with the permit conditions.
4.2.2.3 In addition to the general control on the use of PME during restricted hours, the use of
Specified Powered Mechanical Equipment (SPME) and the undertaking of Prescribed
Construction Work (PCW) during the restricted hours in a Designated Area are also
controlled by the DA-TM. Construction plant or equipment classified as SPME under
the DA-TM includes hand-held breaker, bulldozer, concrete lorry mixer, dump truck
and hand-held vibratory poker. The PCW includes the erection or dismantling of
formwork or scaffolding, hammering, loading, unloading or handling of rubble, wooden
boards, steel bars, wood or scaffolding material.

Blasting
4.2.2.9 There is no statutory procedure or criteria under the NCO and EIAO for assessing the
blasting impacts and is therefore beyond the scope of the EIA. However, the
administrative and procedural control of all blasting operations in Hong Kong is vested
in the Mines Division of the Civil Engineering and Development Department (CEDD).
The Dangerous Goods Ordinance (Cap. 295) also stipulates that no person shall carry
out blasting unless he possesses a valid mine blasting certificate to be issued by the
Mines Division of CEDD. The Superintendent of Mines will review the application on a
case-by-case basis before issuing the Mine Blasting Certificate. Although there is no
statutory noise level for blasting, the noise associated with the removal of debris and
rocks are controlled under the EIAO-TM.

Description of Noise Environment
4.3.1.1 The Project is an approximately 9km long dual three-lane carriage, mainly in the form
of at-grade road, tunnel and viaduct connecting between the interchange of San Tin
Highway and Tsing Long Highway via Ngau Tam Mei to Kwu Tung.
4.3.1.2 Interchanges will be constructed at Yuen Long Highway/Tsing Long Highway, Ngau
Tam Mei Development Area, San Tin Technopole, Fanling Highway and Kwu Tung
North NDA. The noise climate at these interchanges are dictated by the road traffic
noise from their surrounding road network, i.e. noise climate at the interchange at Yuen
Long Highway/Tsing Long Highway is dominated by the road traffic from Yuen Long
Highway and Tsing Long Highway; noise climate at Ngau Tam Mei Development Area
is dictated by the scattered industrial or brownfield operations and from the road traffic
from local roads; noise climate at San Tin Technopole is dictated by the scattered
industrial or brownfield operations and from the road traffic from the local road; and the
noise climate at Kwu Tung North NDA is dictated by the road traffic from the road
network including Fanling Highway.
4.3.1.3 Tunnel will be constructed from Ngau Tam Mei to San Tin Technopole and from San
Tin Technopole to Kwu Tung area. The areas which tunnel passed through are
conservation area at Ngau Tam Mei and Kwu Tung Reservoir respectively, which are
mainly rural in nature. The noise climate at these areas is dictated by scattered
industrial or brownfield operations and from road traffic from local roads.
4.3.1.4 Open road sections will be constructed from Tung Shing Lei to Ngau Tam Mei and
Kwu Tung North. The areas are comprises of greenbelts, comprehensive development
areas, villages, industrial areas and conservation areas. The noise climate at the open
road sections between Tung Shing Lei and Ngau Tam Mei is dictated by Yuen Long
Highway, Tsing Long Highway, San Tam Road and Castle Peak Road – Tam Mi; and
the noise climate along Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area (NTM NDA) and San
Tin Technopole is dictated by scattered industrial or brownfield operations and from
road traffic from local roads. Noise climate for the section at Kwu Tung North is dictated
by Fanling Highway, Castle Peak Road – Chau Tau and Kwu Tung Road.

Assessment Methodology
4.5.1.1 According to Clause 1.2.2 of Appendix C of the EIA Study Brief, a qualitative
assessment is required to demonstrate no adverse construction noise impact would
be associated with the Project by adopting quieter construction method and equipment
and further construction noise mitigation measures during the construction stages. The
general approach of this qualitative construction noise impact assessment, with
reference to Sections 5.3 and 5.4 of Annex 13 of the EIAO-TM and EIAO GN No.
9/2023, is summarized below:
• Determine 300m assessment area from the Project Site boundary which
includes the associated works required under the Project;
• Identify existing, committed and planned NSRs within the assessment area and
assign NAPs on the representative NSRs that would most likely be affected by
noise from the construction works;
• Summarize the construction method for the key construction works;
• Collate the construction plant inventory for the key construction works;
• Evaluate the potential construction noise impact on the NSRs qualitatively;
• Evaluate cumulative construction noise impact from concurrent projects
qualitatively;
• Examine and recommend all practical mitigation measures, such as adoption of
alternative construction methodology, quiet plant, silencer, enclosure, etc., to
alleviate any potential noise impacts as much as practicable with reference to
Annex 13 of the EIAO-TM and EIAO GN No. 9/2023; and
• Propose to submit a Construction Noise Management Plan (CNMP), which
contains quantitative construction noise impact assessment, to the
Environmental Protection Department (EPD).

area for construction noise impact assessment shall include areas within 300m from

Inventory of Noise Sources
4.5.2.4 Section 2 of this EIA Report has described the key project elements and the
associated construction methods. The potential sources of noise impact during the
construction of the Project would be the use of PME for various construction activities.
The main construction works encompass the following:
• Ground investigation (GI) works;
• Site clearance and formation;
• Construction of at-grade roads, viaducts and interchanges;
• Construction of tunnels by drill and blast / drill and break method;
• Construction of Administration Building, Portal Plant Building/ Plant Room/
Control Room; and
• Ancillary works including slope works, adits and associated connection with
existing roads, reprovisioning and reinstatement works, landscaping works,
road lighting, etc.
4.5.2.5 The construction programme currently envisioned does not require the use of
percussive piling. In accordance with the list of good practices and state-of-the-art
technologies within the industry, the construction methods and equipment below can
be employed in this Project:
• Quieter type blade saws and hydraulic crushers for concrete removal during site
clearance;
• Non-explosive chemical expansion agents and hydraulic splitters for concrete
or rock breaking activities;
• Self-compacting concrete instead of vibratory poker for concreting works;
• Quieter piling method by large diameter bored piling to minimize the impact on
existing structures; and
• Off-site concreting works for viaduct construction with pre-cast segments.
4.5.2.6 According to the construction methods envisaged at this stage, the key construction
activities and the associated tentative PMEs have been outlined in Table 4.11 below.
The plant inventory adopted for the assessment have been confirmed by Project

construction plant inventory and the Construction Noise Management Plan (CNMP)
based on the available engineering data and considerations at that time.
4.5.2.7 For the construction of tunnel, Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) is not adopted in view of
cost-effectiveness which requires relatively higher capital cost of initial investment and
limitation on the road alignment (e.g. requiring large turning radius). There is limitation
of site areas for launching and retrieving the TBM. Moreover, tunnel section (circular
shape) created by TBM would necessarily generate more C&D material than section
(horseshoe) created by drill and blast method.

4.5.4.10 Movable noise barriers or noise enclosures would be erected to provide screening from
the construction plant. Noise barriers would be most effective when located
immediately adjacent to the PME and can reduce the noise level by 5 dB(A) for
movable PME and by 10 dB(A) for stationary PME. The Contractor shall be responsible
for design of the noise barrier with due consideration given to the size of the PME and
the requirement of intercepting the line of sight between the NSRs and PME. The
barrier material of movable noise barrier should have at least 10 kg/m2 surface density.
Purpose-built acoustics barrier can be used to screen noise from particular items of
PME or noisy construction activities. The direct line of sight between the PME and the
NSRs should be totally screened by a substantial barrier such that the PME will not be
visible when viewed from any window, door or other opening in any facade of the NSR.
A noise reduction of 10 dB(A) is assumed for purpose-built noise barrier. Full
enclosures can be considered as an alternative to shelter relatively static plant
including generator. The provision of full enclosure is expected to provide 15 dB(A)
noise reduction for static PME. To ensure the above-mentioned noise reduction
performance of the noise barrier, there should be no gap or opening for the noise
barrier/enclosure being constructed by acoustic mats.

Road Traffic Noise
4.9.2.1 A road traffic noise assessment has been conducted according to the requirements in
EIA Study Brief. Mitigation measures, such as LNRS, vertical and cantilevered type
noise barriers as well as at-receiver mitigation measures (acoustic
window/door/balcony) have been recommended to be implemented within the Project
Road extent to fulfil the respective requirements.
Fixed Noise
4.9.3.1 Fixed noise sources impact of the Project has been evaluated according to the
requirements in EIA Study Brief. With the adoption of proposed noise mitigation
measures, including the use of quieter equipment, silencer, barrier, enclosure, etc.,
adverse noise impact arising from fixed noise sources is not anticipated. Nevertheless,
a FNMP, which contains a quantitative fixed noise sources impact assessment,
mitigation measures and monitoring and audit programme, should be submitted prior
to issuance of the tender and before commencement of construction of the proposed
fixed noise sources.
